explanation: Command-line arguments always arrive as Strings, so Double.parseDouble turns each one into a number you can add up. args.length is both the guard for the empty case and the divisor for the average -- checking it first avoids dividing by zero. printf with %.2f formats the result to two decimals, and passing Locale.US keeps the decimal point a dot on machines whose default locale uses a comma.
hints: Handle args.length == 0 first: print the usage line and return, so the rest of the method only ever sees real input.
Total the values in a double accumulator with an enhanced for loop over args, calling Double.parseDouble on each element.
The average is total / args.length -- total is already a double, so this is real division, not integer division.
